_comment: Curated offline cache for demo/package.json, keyed by package@version. References real published advisories (CVE/GHSA IDs) where they exist, used so grading/CI runs are deterministic and don't depend on live network access, rate limits, or a GITHUB_TOKEN. See README 'Offline demo fixtures' section.

colors@1.4.1.summary: No formal CVE was ever filed for this version. In January 2022 the maintainer intentionally sabotaged colors (and the related faker package), pushing an infinite-loop payload as a form of protest, which broke countless downstream builds. It's treated here purely as a behavioral anomaly (single maintainer, an erratic, out-of-pattern release) rather than a CVSS-scored vulnerability - there is no 'fixed version' to upgrade to, since it wasn't a code vulnerability with a patch; remediation is to pin to a pre-incident version (1.4.0) or replace the dependency.

minimist@1.2.0.summary: Prototype pollution in minimist allows an attacker to modify Object.prototype via a crafted __proto__ payload passed to the argument parser.

axios@1.5.0.summary: axios leaks the confidential XSRF-TOKEN cookie value in the Proxy-Authorization header when following a cross-origin redirect, allowing an attacker-controlled proxy target to obtain it.

moment@2.29.1.summary: moment's parsing of certain user-controlled date strings has inadequate complexity, allowing a regular-expression-denial-of-service (ReDoS) attack against applications that pass untrusted input to moment's parser.

xml2js@0.4.19.summary: Prototype pollution in xml2js allows attacker-controlled XML input to modify Object.prototype, potentially leading to denial of service or property injection in the host application.

node-ipc@9.2.1.summary: node-ipc versions 10.1.1 and 9.2.1 through 9.2.2 contained code that, based on the host machine's IP-derived geolocation, either overwrote or deleted arbitrary files on disk (the 2022 'protestware' incident). Treated here as a Critical-severity supply chain compromise, curated with a representative CVSS-equivalent score.

ansi-regex@5.0.0.summary: ansi-regex is vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS): an inefficient regular expression used to match ANSI escape codes can be forced into catastrophic backtracking by a crafted, invalid escape sequence, exhausting CPU on the process parsing it.

glob-parent@5.1.1.summary: The enclosure regex used by glob-parent before 5.1.2 to detect brace/bracket patterns is a non-linear regular expression; a crafted input (e.g. a brace followed by many path separators) triggers catastrophic backtracking, causing a Regular Expression Denial of Service.

json5@2.2.1.summary: The parse method of JSON5 before 2.2.2 does not restrict parsing of keys named __proto__, so a specially crafted JSON5 string can pollute Object.prototype of the resulting object, potentially leading to denial of service or, depending on how the polluted object is later used, further application-level compromise.

word-wrap@1.2.3.summary: word-wrap uses an insecure regular expression when trimming trailing whitespace; a specially crafted input string triggers catastrophic backtracking in that regex, causing a Regular Expression Denial of Service on the process handling it.

tar@6.1.0.summary: node-tar before 6.1.1 insufficiently sanitizes absolute paths inside an archive: a file path with a repeated path root (e.g. multiple leading slashes) has only a single root stripped, so extraction can still resolve to an absolute path outside the intended directory, allowing arbitrary file creation or overwrite.

pyyaml@5.3.1.summary: PyYAML before 5.4 is vulnerable to arbitrary code execution when it processes untrusted YAML through full_load or the FullLoader loader. The python/object/new constructor tag lets an attacker instantiate an arbitrary Python class, including ones from the subprocess module, achieving code execution.

pillow@8.4.0.summary: PIL.ImageMath.eval in Pillow before 9.0.0 allows evaluation of arbitrary expressions, including ones that call Python builtins such as exec, eval, and __import__, allowing arbitrary code execution.

urllib3@1.26.16.summary: urllib3 does not strip the Cookie request header when following a cross origin redirect, leaking any cookie set by the caller to the redirect target, potentially exposing session or authentication tokens to an unrelated domain.

jinja2@3.1.2.summary: The xmlattr filter in Jinja2 before 3.1.3 does not validate keys, so a key containing spaces coming from user input can be used to inject arbitrary HTML attributes into a template, bypassing autoescaping and enabling cross site scripting.

werkzeug@2.2.2.summary: Werkzeug's multipart form data parser before 2.2.3 parses an unlimited number of parts, including file parts. A crafted request with a very large number of parts consumes CPU, memory, or file handles, blocking worker processes or crashing the process, a denial of service.
